name: checkbox-tree

frames.best_why: All branches and leaves are visible at once showing ticked, unticked and partly ticked boxes, with no cursor over them.

tagline: Nested categories where ticking a parent ticks all its children.
summary: A tree of category labels, each with a small square box, nested under thin indent rules. Ticking a parent selects everything beneath it, and a parent with only some children ticked shows a dash.
appearance: A narrow dark list of light grey labels, each led by a small square box and stepped inward from its parent along a faint vertical rule. Ticked boxes are filled white with a dark mark; partly selected branches show a short dash.
behaviour: Clicking a box ticks it and every child under it, and clicking a full branch clears them all. A branch whose children are only partly ticked switches its own box to a dash. Nothing animates.
demo_content: Tech-stack categories: Frontend (React, Vue, Svelte), Backend (Node.js, Python, Go), Database (PostgreSQL, MongoDB).
search_phrases: tree of tick boxes for filters
folder list with squares to tick
partly selected parent shows a dash
use_when: Users pick categories across a hierarchy, and ticking a parent should select everything below it.
avoid_when: The source calls itself a demo with no keyboard or tree semantics, so it is not production ready.
customise: Hand it a tree of nodes plus a renderNode function that draws each row; the parent-child checking logic is internal and all visual styling is left to you.
weight_why: A handful of nested rows and recursive state checks; no animation, timers or canvas.

a11y.note: Each box is labelled and can be toggled by keyboard, but the tree has no tree role, so nesting is announced as a flat run of boxes.

issues: Frame 1 shows the root ticked while some of its children are unticked
No frame shows a keyboard focus ring on any box
polish_why: Clear nesting and sensible state logic, but rows are cramped and the indent rules are faint.
